newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller says revs thru Jan rise 3.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller says revs thru Jan rise 3.8 pct.

text.p: The New York State Comptroller on Friday said that through in the first 10 months of fiscal 1997 all governmental funds, tax collections totaled $30 billion, a 3.8 percent increase over the year-ago period.
However, the extra funds will not be available to pump up spending.

"Because the financial plan was revised with the governor's budget, there is virtually no variance between January results and the governor's financial plan," H. Carl McCall said, in prepared remarks.
And the fiscal monitor, who has said he is considering running as a Democratic candidate for govenor, cautioned that the state seems likely to again fail to approve its budget on time.
"The fiscal year ends in only 45 days, yet there is no sense of urgency in the capitol that the budget must be enacted next month," he added.
Total personal income tax collections rose 4.4 percent to $16.2 billion, though a large share is from last year's surplus.
While tax reductions cut personal income tax witholding 2.5 percent over the same period over the year-ago period, estimated personal income tax payments leaped 18.2 percent.
Nor were those the only increases: sales tax climbed 4.7 percent against the first 10 months of fiscal 1996 and total consumer taxes and fees are 2.5 percent higher at $7.9 billion.
Business taxes gained 3.9 percent to $4.9 billion.
The contribution from other taxes firmed 4.0 percent to $1 billion, a rise outpaced by miscellaneous receipts, which rose 6.4 percent to $7.5 billion, mainly due to one-time revenues.
Disbursements for all governmental funds edged up to $49 billion through January.
